row.evidence: Slab's pricing table ticks SCIM Provisioning and SAML-based SSO only on Business ($12.50/user/mo billed annually) and Enterprise, and the Okta SCIM guide says you must be on the Business or Enterprise plan.
row.notes: New row. Plans: Free (up to 10 users), Startup $6.67, Business $12.50 per user/mo billed annually, Enterprise custom (at least 100 users). SCIM and SAML SSO start at Business, one tier above the Startup team plan; the 'Single Sign On' row ticked on every plan is Google/Slack/Microsoft sign-in, not SAML. SCIM is documented only through Slab's Okta and OneLogin catalogue apps (SAML must be configured first); no generic SCIM endpoint, Entra, Google Workspace or JumpCloud provisioning is documented. Slab's GraphQL API and webhooks are Business+ but are documented as content APIs; whether they manage users could not be confirmed (Apollo Studio schema did not render). Deactivated users stop being billed (credit for remaining term).

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: GraphQL API and webhooks included; Audit Logs row is not ticked on the pricing table although the help centre says audit logs are on Business (see conflicts).

scim.notes: SCIM is set up only through Slab's own Okta and OneLogin catalogue apps; Slab does not publish a SCIM base URL, version or generic setup guide.

auth.token_source: Slab Team settings > Integrations > Okta (or OneLogin) > Provisioning tab > enable SCIM and copy SCIM API Token

operations.notes: Deleting a user in Okta deactivates them in Slab rather than deleting them. Update method (PUT/PATCH) not documented.

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivated users can no longer log in; their published posts stay and ownership is transferred to another teammate or Slab Bot. A credit is issued for the remaining subscription time, and billing counts only users who can log in. Reactivated users must rejoin topics and groups.

custom.how: userType attribute (admin, guest or standard user) mapped from Okta assignments or OneLogin rules; groups parameter in OneLogin maps roles to Slab Groups.

attributes.notes: Slab does not publish a full attribute list; name and title are named as synced fields, userName is the matching key.

roles.how: userType attribute sets standard user, admin or guest; OneLogin roles map to Slab Groups via a rule.

limitations.text: Username changes are not supported; changing the Okta username can break the user.
Users or groups assigned in Okta before SCIM was enabled are not updated or deactivated until unassigned and reassigned.
The IdP is the source of truth: Slab-side edits to name or title and to pushed group membership are overwritten.
Push-group members join Slab groups as regular members; group owners must be set in Slab.
OneLogin provisioning needs OneLogin's Advanced Directory add-on.

user_api.notes: Slab has a GraphQL API (Business and Enterprise) documented as a content API acting as Slab Bot. Whether it exposes user management could not be checked: the Apollo Studio schema page did not render headlessly and the endpoint refuses unauthenticated introspection.

auth.notes: Admins copy an API token from Team settings > Developer; the auth scheme is not described on the help page.

audit_log_api.notes: Audit logs are viewable in Team settings (Business and Enterprise per the help centre); no API export is documented.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML and SCIM, and Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking as checked (read from page markup).

entra.notes: No Slab tutorial in Microsoft Learn's SaaS app tutorial index; Slab lists Microsoft/Office 365/Azure AD sign-in among SSO options but documents no Entra SAML or provisioning setup.

google.notes: Slab supports Google sign-in; no Google Workspace SAML or provisioning app documented.

onelogin.notes: From Slab's own OneLogin guide (OneLogin catalogue not loaded).

jumpcloud.notes: jumpcloud.com returned 403 to curl and WebFetch.
